prerequisites: It is recommended not to undertake this subject until having achieved the most complete possible vision of the technical disciplines taught in the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering that have as their object the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to manage the activities subject to the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Ability for the prevention of occupational risks and protection of the health and safety of workers and users.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Understand the legal and ethical requirements and implications of professional engineering practice, particularly in project development.
Know the characteristics of projects, their life cycle, and the technical, economic, safety, environmental, legal, social, and ethical conditions to consider in them.

Define the scope of a project and plan the deadlines and costs of all necessary tasks to carry it out, and monitor the progress and supervision of the work to be done in a project, keeping the initial planning in mind.
Clearly present and adequately justify the solutions adopted in a project, preparing the associated documents that allow its contracting and execution.
Understand the structure and functions of a technical office, as well as develop and improve a work method.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory Practices (EV-3). Exercises performed in class

assessment_rules: To pass the ordinary call, a minimum of 5 points out of 10 must be obtained in each of the three parts (EV-1, EV-2, EV-3). If these minimums are achieved, the final grade will be calculated as: Grade = 0.4 * EV-1 + 0.35 * EV-2 + 0.25 * EV-3. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For EV-2, the average of the two works is taken, provided each work's grade is above 4.0; otherwise, the EV-2 grade is the minimum of the average and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, grades above 5 obtained in the ordinary call for EV-1, EV-2, or EV-3 can be carried over; if the student retakes the test, the new grade will be used.
